author: assistant-drafted, pending operator verification
constraints: The string holds between 1 and one hundred thousand characters and contains only the letters A and B.
edge_cases: The first and last pieces can never be removed because they do not have a piece on both sides. A player may only remove a piece of their own colour, never the other player's.
input_semantics: One parameter, colors, a string in which each character is either the letter A or the letter B.
load_bearing: Both neighbours must match, not one. The piece removed must match its own neighbours in colour. Alice moves first, and a player who cannot move loses rather than passing.
method_behaviour: The method accepts the string and returns a boolean. It does not print and does not return a count of moves.
objective: Two players alternately remove letters from a row of coloured pieces under a strict neighbour condition; decide whether the first player wins when both play as well as possible.
output_semantics: A boolean: true when Alice wins, false when Bob wins.
required_operation: The row is given as text of the letters A and B. Alice moves first and may remove a piece coloured A only when both of the pieces immediately beside it are also coloured A. Bob may remove a piece coloured B only when both pieces immediately beside it are also coloured B. Players alternate and a player unable to make a legal removal loses immediately. Report whether Alice wins.
